title: `Vat.fold` / `Vat.suck` / `Pot.drip` — single-key governance can unilaterally mint unbacked Dai
impact: `Vat.suck(u, v, rad)` mints `dai[v]` and `sin[u]` with no cap; `Vat.fold` increases `ilk.rate` and mints `dai[vow]` proportionally to `Art`. A single compromised `ward` (e.g. the `Pot`, `Jug`, or `End`) can inflate `debt`/`vice` arbitrarily or drive stability fees to extreme values (`Jug.file("duty")` has no upper bound). This is by design in Maker, but the absence of rate caps, mint caps, or timelocks on these paths is a material centralization risk.
